findings.description: Focus fix correctly implemented: onAccessibilityEvent now uses view.hasWindowFocus() instead of view.isFocused (line 230), startFocusWatchdog uses hasWindowFocus() (line 983), watchdog interval tightened from 2000ms to 150ms (line 1261), and MotionCaptureView.onWindowFocusChanged added for immediate reclaim (lines 1231-1238). All changes match the user intent exactly and address the reported button unreliability root cause.

MotionCaptureView comment claims digital buttons route through the focused view as primary path ('the a11y onKeyEvent path loses the race'), but onKeyEvent (line 311) returns true for all mapped keys, consuming them before MotionCaptureView ever sees them. The user intent states digital buttons are 'dispatched through the same MotionCaptureView', but the a11y filter handles them instead. Either the comment is misleading, or the architecture doesn't match the stated intent. This could mean the focus fix for digital buttons is incomplete if the a11y filter path doesn't benefit from the watchdog.

VoiceBridgeServer generates per-instance authToken (line 46) but token is never exposed to any client — started in ControllerAccessibilityService.onServiceConnected() but not logged, stored, or shared via IPC. Comment states 'Give this only to the trusted in-process caller' but no mechanism exists to pass it. The /voice and /speak endpoints require this token (checked at line 124) but no legitimate caller can authenticate. Pre-existing issue (F1/HYS-3), now in a new file in this diff.

REV=3 migration (lines 70-78) discards ALL user-customized button mappings from legacy profiles (rev < 3), keeping only tuning values (sensitivity/deadzone/cursorEnabled/invertScroll). This is a breaking data-loss change for existing users. While acknowledged as acceptable for AntiMicroX parity in comments, it must be explicitly documented in release notes so users know their custom mappings will be reset. Pre-existing issue (F2/HYS-4), now in a new file in this diff.

PttController implements double-press cancel: a second ACTION_DOWN while isHeld=true calls onCancel() and resets state (lines 28-35). This is new behavior not present in the Linux ptt_pynput.py original. A user holding the trigger who accidentally presses again (or a noisy trigger edge) will cancel their recording without warning. With hysteresis fix, accidental double-press from noise is less likely (requires crossing 0.5->0.25->0.5), but intentional/accidental double-press still triggers cancel. Pre-existing issue (F3/HYS-6/RV6), now in a new file in this diff.

Browser and IPTV preset profiles have actions mapped to NONE with misleading labels (e.g., browser: X=Reload mapped to NONE at line 105; IPTV: LT=◀◀ mapped to NONE at line 137, RT=▶▶ mapped to voiceTrigger at line 138 with mismatched label). Comments acknowledge this as 'label/action-mismatch precedent' but users will see labels that don't match actual behavior.

MAX_RECORDING_MS hardcoded to 30 seconds (line 1263) with auto-cancel behavior. No user configuration for this limit. For long-form dictation this may be too restrictive. Consider making it configurable or at least documented.

testing_summary: Build compiles successfully (./gradlew compileDebugKotlin). No test suite exists in this repo; changes cannot be live-verified in this sandboxed environment (no KVM/emulator, no physical gamepad) — same limitation acknowledged and accepted in prior runs.
risk_rationale: Core focus fix is correct and low-risk, but the branch introduces multiple new files (VoiceBridgeServer, PttController, ContextSwitcher, ProfileSerializer) with design decisions that need clarification: auth token never exposed, breaking profile migration, double-press cancel behavior, preset action/label mismatches, and a potential architecture mismatch between MotionCaptureView comment and actual key event routing. These are not bugs in the focus fix itself but represent significant new behavior requiring product decisions.
